free_tier.stated: Starter 50 GB ₹20/mo; Freelancer 100 GB ₹35/mo; 500 GB ₹100/mo; Studio Pro 1 TB ₹150/mo (or ₹1,650/yr); 25 GB free forever. Enterprise pooled storage on request.

egress.terms: Claimed free. The business page is titled «Eliminate Egress Fees» and argues against providers «that charge hidden egress fees», and the pricing JSON-LD implies flat-rate. But no numbered egress allowance, no fair-use clause and no overage rate is published anywhere on the site — so the claim cannot be falsified from outside.

tooling: None documented. No public API, no WebDAV, no S3 endpoint, no rclone backend, no CLI. The product page describes «Zero-Knowledge Personal Vault», AES-256-GCM client-side encryption, mobile sync and a web UI. This is the disqualifying gap.
chaining: Per-account consumer plans; no documented route that uses several accounts and no API to automate one.
limits_note: Zero programmatic access. The entire site is SEO-shaped: multiple near-identical 2026 comparison articles on its own domain ranking itself #1, with an «Independent Industry Audit» framing. The 1 TB price is also contradicted by its own pricing page rendering an empty shell to every reader that reached it — /pricing, /pricing.html and /cloud-storage-pricing all resolved to the same 37-word stub with `confidence: low`.
reliability_note: Record as UNVERIFIED, not qualifying. Three independent signals of thinness: (1) the site 403s a plain `curl` with a bare HTML body and no content negotiation; (2) the actual /pricing page returns a 37-word synthetic stub to every extraction path tried (firecrawl, direct fetch) while the marketing articles are fully readable — i.e. the price exists only in prose, never in a page that renders a table; (3) no API, no status page, no company registration details. ₹150/TB/mo is ~1/17th of AWS and 1/6th of Utho's best tier, which is not a price a real 1 TB Indian host can hold.
